# Shared-facet perturbation: strict cap-menu separation and an exact paying hinge

The R4 bad-profile obstruction is not robust under a natural nonaffine
common-facet perturbation. This note proves both sides of that statement:
the desired separation of its nine simplest cap competitors is feasible,
but the perturbed profile immediately admits a convex potential of
efficiency 2/3. No global-criticality assertion is made for the perturbed
caps, and no selected-circuit counterexample is claimed.

## 1. The actual compatible family

Use the base D4 and its 31 integer points P from the exact R4 theorem. Let

    ell0=-z1-z2, ell1=2z1-z2, ell2=2z2-z1,
    B(z)=ell0(z)^2+ell1(z)^2+ell2(z)^2.

Let K be a triangle of area V with barycentric coordinates lambda_j.
For 0<e<1/96 define the actual convex body

    C_e={z in D4, sum lambda_j=1,
                    lambda_j>=e ell_j(z)^2 for j=0,1,2}.       (1)

Each displayed inequality is convex in the full physical variables: its
left-side defining convex function is e ell_j(z)^2-lambda_j(x).
Moreover B(z)<=96 on D4, because B is convex and has value96 at its three
vertices. Thus every projected point has a positive-area fiber. The body
is compact, convex and has nonempty interior; its integer projection is
exactly P. Its fibers have the same three oriented facet normals, but
nonaffine centroids and varying homothety factors:

    r_z=1-eB(z),
    |K_z|=V r_z^2,
    lambda_j(g_z)=e ell_j(z)^2+r_z/3.               (2)

The origin fiber is exactly K. Its centroid g is the source under study.
This is a genuine convex perturbation, not independent prescribed fiber
motions lacking midpoint compatibility.

## 2. Nine exact cap masses and diagonal stationarity

Index base direction by j and continuous barycentric coordinate by k:

    H_jk={lambda_k(x)-1/3+ell_j(z)>=0}.             (3)

For every j,k, the twelve positive-offset fibers are strictly full,
the sixteen negative-offset fibers strictly empty, and the three
zero-offset fibers proper. These statements hold throughout the stated
e interval, since all lambda coordinates lie in [0,1].

For each j, finite exact enumeration of the complete base gives

    sum_(ell_j>0) B=360,
    sum_(ell_j>0) B^2=18144.

The zero slice consists of 0 and opposite integer vectors. Its B values
are 0,18,18. On those two nonzero points ell_j^2=0 and the other two squares
are both9. A continuous coordinate-k cap at threshold1/3 has area

    V[2/3-e(B-ell_k^2)]^2.

Consequently the three diagonal masses are exactly

    Q_e/V=40/3-768e+18792e^2,                      (4)

whereas each of the six off-diagonal masses equals

    40/3-744e+18306e^2.

Their difference is

    24e-486e^2>0.                                 (5)

The diagonal caps still have full mixed section centroid (0,g), exactly,
not just to first order. On their two nonzero zero-slice fibers the two
nonfixed barycentric lower bounds are equal, so the cut-segment midpoint
is g. The opposite base points have identical section lengths. The origin
section also has midpoint g. This proves both continuous and integer
section-centroid equations. The three total coareas are equal, namely
4V-72Ve, giving normalized response weights theta_j=1/3. All other
fiber traces are strictly saturated, so these cap data are regular.

Their margins sum to zero, hence they cover the ambient space and give
global raw depth at most Q_e. The diagonal vertex-permutation group of
base and continuous triangles preserves C_e. Its orbit average is (0,g),
so (0,g) is a global deepest point by convexity of depth regions. Neither
fact proves that its depth is Q_e: a different oblique cap may have smaller
mass. The current claim is exact stationarity, common mass, and separation
from the six displayed competitors, not all-normal criticality.

For comparison, the first-order formula for arbitrary sampled-convex
facet offsets b_l(z) and source displacement lambda_k(y)=1/3+e y_k is

    (mass H_jk)'/V=R_j+(4/3) sum_(ell_j=0)b_k-4y_k,
    R_j=-2 sum_(ell_j>0)sum_l b_l
                    -(4/3)sum_(ell_j=0)sum_l b_l. (6)

Our actual quadratic choice has diagonal zero-slice sum0 and off-diagonal
sum18, realizing the positive first-order gap24 in (5).

## 3. A single affine hinge exposes a paying fiber facet

Let n0 be the common outward unit normal of the facets having lower
barycentric bound on lambda0. On that facet of fiber z, write

    s=ell0(z), t=ell1(z), ell2(z)=-s-t,
    lambda0=e s^2,
    lambda1<=1-e s^2-e(s+t)^2.

Consider the affine physical function

    L_e(z,x)=lambda1(x)-2e ell1(z)
            -6[lambda0(x)+4e ell0(z)+4e]-(1-7e).  (7)

Substitution into the facet inequalities gives

    L_e <= e[6h-7h^2-(s+t+1)^2],  h=s+2.         (8)

Here h is an integer. If h!=0, then 6h-7h^2<=-1. If h=0, the only way
the remaining square can vanish is s=-2,t=1, which solves to z=(1,1).
Every other integer base on this slice has the square at least1 (in fact
at least9 for this P). Therefore

    L_e<=-e on every n0-facet except the one at z_*=(1,1).

At z_*, its exact facet formula is

    L_e=lambda1-(1-5e),
    e<=lambda1<=1-5e.

Thus [L_e+e/2]_+ vanishes on all the other actual n0-facets and is positive
on a nonzero-length portion of this one. No limiting concentration or
unproved ability to isolate an interior base is used.

Choose a continuous nonnegative function psi on the unit-normal sphere
with psi(n0)=1 and psi(n1)=psi(n2)=0, where n1,n2 are the other two common
facet normals. For example the product of squared distances from n1,n2,
normalized to have value1 at n0, has these properties. Define

    Phi(n,z,x)=psi(n)[L_e(z,x)+e/2]_+.              (9)

For each fixed n this is nonnegative and convex in the physical variables.
It is continuous, and its integral against the actual boundary measure
is finite and strictly positive. On that boundary bundle it is supported
only on the n0-facet of the single fiber z_*.

At z_* the three offsets are (-2,1,1). The diagonal cap H_00 is strictly
empty, and H_11,H_22 are strictly full. Hence the diagonal profile

    W=(1/3)(1_H00+1_H11+1_H22)

is identically 2/3 throughout that fiber. Equations (7)--(9) therefore
prove the exact equality

    integral Phi W d eta / integral Phi d eta=2/3. (10)

The boundary facet orientation stays fixed as e decreases to zero, but
the slopes of the exposing potential in physical coordinates exploit
arbitrarily small support offsets. Consequently no uniform upper
semicontinuity of the supremum over the entire convex-potential cone can
be assumed. At e=0 the prescribed R4 profile has optimum40/93; for every
e>0 in this actual family its optimum is at least2/3.

## 4. Scope for favorable-circuit selection

This construction shows that breaking continuous permutation symmetry
can separate the diagonal cap menu at first order and still fail to retain
its low potential efficiency. It rejects the proposed robustness step
for this explicit common-facet deformation. It neither proves that every
symmetry-breaking deformation admits a paying hinge nor proves that the
diagonal caps are the true minimizing caps after deformation. Such
all-normal and full-cone assertions require separate arguments.
